Prioritizing due diligence and manager selection can be key to building an allocation to alternatives that enhances your portfolio’s diversification and outperformance potential. Head of Investment Strategy, J.P.Morgan Wealth Management. Alternative investments – like private equity and credit, hedge funds and real assets – can help investors solve for many of these challenges and access a broader set of opportunities, but there are a few crucial considerations to keep in mind when allocating to them. Read on for why we think investors should carefully select the portfolio managers with whom they deploy capital, weigh the trade-offs between evergreen and traditional drawdown funds and understand the implications of alternative investment allocations for portfolio risk exposures.

This article provides essential tips for new investors to navigate the world of alternative investments. Navigating the world of alternative investments can be exciting, but it also requires careful planning and understanding of the unique risks involved. Here are some essential tips for new investors who are looking to explore alternative assets:. • **Understand the asset class:** Each type of alternative investment—such as real estate, private equity, hedge funds, commodities, or cryptocurrencies—comes with its own characteristics, potential returns, and risks. For example, Real Estate- Real estate is a physical, tangible asset, unlike stocks or bonds, which are intangible. **• Understand the risk profile of each asset:** Many alternative investments can be illiquid, volatile, or highly leveraged, so it’s essential to evaluate how much risk you’re willing to take.

An investment portfolio can paint a clear picture of a person and their goals for the future. Traditional investors might limit their selections to asset classes such as stocks, bonds, and cash. However, for those savvy investors looking to both embrace innovation and fill gaps in their portfolios, there are other options. Alternative investments are any disparate asset that is not the traditional publicly-traded option of a bond, stock, cash, etc. However, some alternative investments are still considered a common vehicle to pursue, such as real estate or commodities. Some typical alternative investments are hedge funds, cryptocurrency, private equity, venture capital, derivative contracts, managed futures, and tangible assets such as antiques and art. There may also be different lengths of time when the money is locked in before an investor can access it. When diving into alternative investments, you want to be sure to establish an alternative strategy suited to your needs and desired level of risk.
